top_signals.title: Lilly to Buy Merida for $2.88 Billion in Autoimmune Push
top_signals.summary:
Eli Lilly & Co. plans to buy Merida Biosciences Inc. for as much as $2.88 billion in cash to expand in autoimmune and allergic diseases, part of an effort to build beyond the weight-loss and diabetes markets that made it the largest pharmaceutical company in the world.

Lilly has been on a record spending spree, having announced more than $20 billion in deals so far in 2026. The drugmaker has been using the windfall from its Zepbound and Mounjaro shots to diversify its pipeline, mainly targeting medicines in earlier stages as it seeks to position itself to develop the next blockbuster medicine.

For more, we speak with Michelle Cortez, Bloomberg News Senior Editor for Global Business. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Head for Best August Since 2004
top_signals.summary: Emerging-market stocks are heading for their biggest August advance since 2004 as the rally broadens beyond the biggest artificial-intelligence stocks and gets a boost from commodities riding on the dollar-debasement trade.

top_signals.title: UBS Can Meet Half of New Capital Need With AT1s, Lawmakers Say
top_signals.summary: A key panel of the Swiss parliament backed a compromise proposal on UBS Group AG’s capital requirements that would allow them to meet 50% of the new amount with debt, handing an interim win to the Zurich-based bank.

top_signals.title: The travel shoulder season is shrinking — and so are the savings
top_signals.summary: Traveling during the shoulder season has traditionally been a reliable way to save money on many destinations. But those savings are dwindling.

top_signals.title: Contecon Manzanillo Ready for Ultra Large Container Ships
top_signals.summary: Contecon Manzanillo S.A. de C.V. (CMSA), International Container Terminal Services, Inc.'s (ICTSI) Mexican unit, has paved the way for the Port of Manzanillo to accommodate ultra large container vessels after receiving the go-ahead to handle ships with drafts of up to 15.5 meters.
